newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat says Hebron delay "direct threat" to peace.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says Hebron delay "direct threat" to peace.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Monday further delays in negotiations with Israel on a long-overdue troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron would pose a "direct threat" to Middle East peace moves.
"No doubt if matters continue in this way it will pose a direct threat to the peace process not only on the Palestinian track but in the entire region," Arafat told reporters in self-ruled Gaza.

Arafat was speaking a joint news conference with Qatari Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim al-Thani, who reiterated during his first visit to the Palestinian autonomous enclave that the Gulf emirate would freeze normalisation of ties with Israel unless peace talks moved forward.

Israeli-PLO talks on Hebron, home to 400 Jewish settlers and 100,000 Palestinians, are stalemated over Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's insistence his troops be allowed to enter parts of the city slated to fall under PLO control in "hot pursuit" of suspected guerrillas.
Netanyahu on Monday again accused Arafat of holding up a Hebron deal.

"My impression is that there is a deliberate decision on the Palestinian side not to conclude the talks, to delay possibly with the belief that the blame would be placed at Israel's doorstep," he told reporters.
